record.prompt: Our API gateway runs 4 worker processes (deploy/server.conf) and limits each API key to 100 requests a minute in gateway/limits.py. Read https://docs.quillon.example/config and tell me whether a key really gets 100 per minute overall, or more.

base_changes.keywords: quillon, rate limit, backend, worker processes, tallyd
base_changes.content: Quillon 1.8 rate limiter (docs.quillon.example/config, re-read 2026-10-28): the default memory backend keeps counters per process, so an application with N worker processes lets a key make up to N times the configured rate; a limit shared by all processes needs backend="tally", url="tally://host:7070" pointing at a tallyd server. record.final_answer:
A key can get more than 100 per minute: up to **400 per minute** with your current setup.

**Why:**
- `gateway/limits.py` creates `Limiter(rate="100/minute", key="api_key")` without a `backend`, so it uses the default `memory` backend.
- The Quillon 1.8 docs (https://docs.quillon.example/config) say the `memory` backend keeps its counters inside each process. Each process counts on its own, so "an application with N worker processes lets a key make up to N times the configured rate."
- `deploy/server.conf` sets `workers = 4`, and you're on `quillon==1.8.2` (`requirements.txt`), which is the version those docs cover. So the ceiling is 4 × 100 = **400 requests per minute per key**.

Whether a client actually reaches 400 depends on how requests are spread across the workers. 400 is the upper limit, not a guarantee. A key whose requests keep landing on one worker would be cut off near 100.

**One more thing (my inference, not stated in the docs):** the docs say the windows are fixed and reset at the start of each clock minute. That means a client can use up a full allowance just before a reset and another just after. So within any 60-second stretch spanning a reset, a key could get up to about twice the per-minute limit, roughly 800 across 4 workers.

**To get a true 100/minute overall:** the docs say to switch to the shared backend, for example `Limiter(rate="100/minute", key="api_key", backend="tally", url="tally://<host>:7070")`. That needs a running tallyd server. With a single worker the per-process limit would hold, but you'd lose concurrency. I haven't changed any code.

I updated an existing note in memory with this reading of the Quillon docs, adding the fixed-window detail. The note already had the per-process finding from a reading on 2026-08-12.
